sources.text:
What are the admission documents?
Admission documents for undergraduate applicants require the following:
A completed online application form.
The official final high school transcript (stamped).
Thanawya Amma, or the IGCSE certificates must be stamped by The British Council, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and General Examinations Department - if the school is inside of Egypt; however, if the school is outside of Egypt, the certificates must be stamped by The British Council, Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

A computerized birth certificate.

request.question: للتقديم لهندسة النيل بالـIG، عندي المواد المطلوبة في O level ومعايا AS Math بدرجة D. لازم أجيب A level كمان؟

result.answer:
عشان تقدمي في School of Engineering and Applied Sciences بالـ IG، المطلوب هو 8 مواد O-Level بتقدير لا يقل عن C، لازم يكون من ضمنهم (English, Maths, Physics, Chemistry). وبالنسبة لمادة الـ Math، مطلوب منك مادة واحدة بس تكون AS أو AL Math بتقدير لا يقل عن D [1] [2].

بناءً على المتطلبات، وجودك على AS Math بدرجة D كافي كبديل لـ AL Math في حالة تقديمك لـ Engineering & Applied Sciences، ومش لازم تاخدي A-level عشان متطلبات القبول الأساسية [1] [2].

التفاصيل والتحديثات على الصفحات الرسمية: [IGCSE](https://nu.edu.eg/admission-requirement-and-documents).

## Banque Du Caire Scholarship
Banque du Caire
is offering full scholarships to Egyptian students from all over Egypt applying for undergraduate studies at Nile University at
the School of Information Technology and Computer Science
and
School of Biotechnology
, covering the entire duration of the study.
## Eligibility Criteria:
Graduated this year with a High School degree from Thanaweya Amma (Science and Math division), STEM, or Nile Schools with strong academic performance.
Satisfying admission requirements for the Supreme Council of Universities and Nile University, including English language proficiency.
Demonstrate a strong record of extra-curricular activities, research, innovation, creativity, entrepreneurship abilities, and participation in philanthropic activities
## Scholarship Policy:
High academic progress toward completion of degree requirements. A scholarship recipient is required to maintain a minimum 3.0 GPA throughout the study. Failure to maintain the required GPA will result in losing their place in the scholarship program.

sources.title: International Baccalaureate (IB) — Admission Requirements and Documents | NU
sources.text:
International Baccalaureate (IB)
Applicant should have completed the Baccalaureate diploma degree and satisfied its general requirements. Transfer credit may be granted. Students should have 6 subjects, following these roles: 3 subjects at a higher level and 3 subjects at a standard level.
For Engineering & Applied Sciences ,Information Technology & Computer Science, and Energy and Environmental Engineering School majors: Math and Physics at a higher level are required.
For Biotechnology majors: Chemistry and Biology at a higher level are required.
For Business majors: any 3 subjects at a higher level plus the standard level.
The minimum accepted point is (24).
N.B. Students should have passed the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge subjects.

sources.title: American Diploma — Admission Requirements and Documents | NU
sources.text:
American Diploma
Nile University considers the admission of a minimum cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.0 (on a scale of 4.0). Students who have scored high on Advanced Placement (AP) courses may be granted transfer credits.
The score mentioned below might be subject to change as per the Ministry of Higher Education and the SCU instructions.
Business School: 8 subjects from GPA certificate including English and Maths, along with EST 1, ACT 1 and SAT 1 with a minimum score of 800 and above.
Biotechnology School: 8 subjects from GPA certificate including English, Maths, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, along with EST 1, ACT 1 and SAT 1 with a minimum score of 800 and above.
Engineering and Computer Science School: 8 subjects from GPA certificate including English, Maths, Physics, and Chemistry, along with EST 1, ACT 1 and SAT 1 with a minimum score of 800, and EST 2 with a minimum score of 900.

## The Journey of
## UGRF
Nile University organizes the semi-annual research forum for the undergraduate students periodically, as it is held once at the end of each semester. The research forum for students is one of the most important features of Nile University as a scientific research university and reflects the university’s plan for learning through innovation and applying research.
##
All university students from various schools participate in the forum. The forum includes the provision of scientific research from the students for evaluation and publishing, in addition to research projects for students of different academic years and graduation projects for final year students.

sources.text:
International Baccalaureate (IB)
Applicant should have completed the Baccalaureate diploma degree and satisfied its general requirements. Transfer credit may be granted. Students should have 6 subjects, following these roles: 3 subjects at a higher level and 3 subjects at a standard level.
For Engineering & Applied Sciences ,Information Technology & Computer Science, and Energy and Environmental Engineering School majors: Math and Physics at a higher level are required.
For Biotechnology majors: Chemistry and Biology at a higher level are required.
For Business majors: any 3 subjects at a higher level plus the standard level.
The minimum accepted point is (24).
N.B. Students should have passed the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge subjects.

request.question: معايا شهادة كندية وعايز بيوتكنولوجي النيل. Biology في grade 12 بس كفاية؟

result.answer:
بخصوص دراسة الـ Biotechnology في Nile University، الـ program بيقدم تخصصين هما Applied Biotechnology و Bioinformatics [1] [2]. بالنسبة لمتطلبات القبول، الـ requirements بتختلف حسب نوع الشهادة؛ لو الشهادة هي IGCSE، لازم تقدم 8 مواد بـ minimum grade "C" أو "4"، ولازم يكون من ضمنهم English و Maths و Physics و Chemistry و Biology [8]. لو الشهادة هي IB، لازم تكون خلصت الـ Baccalaureate diploma ومعاك 6 مواد (3 في مستوى أعلى و 3 في مستوى قياسي)، ولازم يكون Chemistry و Biology في مستوى أعلى (higher level) [6].

بما إنك معاك شهادة كندية، الـ information المتاحة مش بتحدد الـ equivalence بتاعها للـ IGCSE أو الـ IB، لكن الـ Biotechnology school بتطلب وجود مواد معينة زي Chemistry و Biology [6] [8]. الـ documents المطلوبة للـ undergraduate applicants بتشمل الـ online application، والـ transcript الموثق، وشهادة الميلاد المميكنة [9] [10].

التفاصيل والتحديثات على الصفحات الرسمية: [Biotechnology Program](https://nu.edu.eg/academics/undergraduate-programs/biotechnology) · [International Baccalaureate  IB](https://nu.edu.eg/admission-requirement-and-documents) · [What are the admission documents?](https://itcs.nu.edu.eg/apply-now).

sources.title: Eligibility Criteria — Sawiris Distinction Scholarship for Public High School Graduates | NU
sources.text:
Eligibility Criteria
Egyptian national residing in Egypt (dual nationality holders are not given priority).
Graduate of an Egyptian public Thanaweya Amma school in 2026/2027 with a score of 90% or higher.
Proof of application to the chosen academic program and confirmation of meeting all program prerequisites. Applicants to English-taught programs must demonstrate the minimum required English proficiency.
Must not have lived abroad for more than three years.
Must commit to working in Egypt for three years after graduation, and to completing military service where applicable.
Priority is given to applicants demonstrating financial need, academic excellence, extracurricular engagement, and Takaful and Karama Program beneficiaries.
Open to students from all governorates, with priority given to applicants from Fayoum, Minya, As

request.question: I'm applying to Nile as a non-Egyptian. Is submitting NU's own form enough, or is there a separate government nomination step?

result.answer:
For non-Egyptian students, submitting the university's own application form is not the only step; a government nomination is required. You must first apply through the "Study in Egypt" portal (ادرس في مصر) to receive a nomination letter from the ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research (Foreign Students Department) before completing the application process at Nile University [1] [6].

Official pages for details and updates: [Application Steps](https://nu.edu.eg/office-international-affairs) · [Non Egyptian Students](https://nu.edu.eg/admission-requirement-and-documents).

sources.title: Student Exchange Programs — Student Exchange | NU
sources.text:
Student Exchange Programs
Nile University prepares undergraduates students for their future careers with a key focus on internationality; all study programs are in English and provide students with the management tools and leadership skills required to succeed on the multicultural stage of today's global market. Nile University’s degree programs are state-accredited and certified internationally.
Moreover, Nile University academic programs adopt the credit hour system which allows for easy transfer of credits from other institutions.
Nile University offers Exchange programs in the areas of:
Engineering and Applied Science
Business Administration
Information Technologies and Computer Science
Biotechnology
Nile University allows students to enroll for one semester abroad at international partner universities.

sources.title: International Baccalaureate (IB) — Admission Requirements and Documents | NU
sources.text:
International Baccalaureate (IB)
Applicant should have completed the Baccalaureate diploma degree and satisfied its general requirements. Transfer credit may be granted. Students should have 6 subjects, following these roles: 3 subjects at a higher level and 3 subjects at a standard level.
For Engineering & Applied Sciences ,Information Technology & Computer Science, and Energy and Environmental Engineering School majors: Math and Physics at a higher level are required.
For Biotechnology majors: Chemistry and Biology at a higher level are required.
For Business majors: any 3 subjects at a higher level plus the standard level.
The minimum accepted point is (24).
N.B. Students should have passed the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge subjects.

or “4”

sources.title: Eligibility Criteria — Sawiris Distinction Scholarship for Public High School Graduates | NU
sources.text:
Eligibility Criteria
Egyptian national residing in Egypt (dual nationality holders are not given priority).
Graduate of an Egyptian public Thanaweya Amma school in 2026/2027 with a score of 90% or higher.
Proof of application to the chosen academic program and confirmation of meeting all program prerequisites. Applicants to English-taught programs must demonstrate the minimum required English proficiency.
Must not have lived abroad for more than three years.
Must commit to working in Egypt for three years after graduation, and to completing military service where applicable.
Priority is given to applicants demonstrating financial need, academic excellence, extracurricular engagement, and Takaful and Karama Program beneficiaries.
Open to students from all governorates, with priority given to applicants from Fayoum, Minya, Assiut, Sohag, and Qena.

## About Program
Master of Science in Mechatronics Engineering is one of the few interdisciplinarities serving diverse domains of application and industry. It integrates mechanical, electronics, control, and computer engineering to develop new end-user products, production systems and automated service establishments that incorporate all those interfaces together.
Read More
## Skills
## The set of skills that MECT students will acquire are the following:
Students completing program requirements at Nile University shall be accredited the Master’s degree from Nile University and are also able to obtain a dual degree with one of the three EU member universities (NU/HSKA – NU/UNIOVI – NU/ENSMM), by spending one year at Nile University and the second year at one of the three EU partner institutions.
Mastering existing Mechatronics Technologies and the ability to improve, upgrade or even renovate them, to achieve host industry objectives.

sources.text:
## program/master-science-mechatronics-engineering
## About Program
Master of Science in Mechatronics Engineering is one of the few interdisciplinarities serving diverse domains of application and industry. It integrates mechanical, electronics, control, and computer engineering to develop new end-user products, production systems and automated service establishments that incorporate all those interfaces together.
Read More
## Skills
## The set of skills that MECT students will acquire are the following:
Students completing program requirements at Nile University shall be accredited the Master’s degree from Nile University and are also able to obtain a dual degree with one of the three EU member universities (NU/HSKA – NU/UNIOVI – NU/ENSMM), by spending one year at Nile University and the second year at one of the three EU partner institutions.
Mastering existing Mechatronics Technologies and the ability to improve, upgrade or even renovate them, to achieve host industry objectives.

16453

sources.title: Do I need an English language qualification test to apply for NU? — FAQs | NU
sources.text:
Do I need an English language qualification test to apply for NU?
All applying students must show proof of English proficiency by achieving the level indicated in one of three testing alternatives below:
A score of 61 or above in the IBT (Internet-based TOEFL).
A score of 6 or above in the IELTS taken at the British Council.
A score of B1 or above in the Oxford exam (no retakes for this exam and is costs 300 EGP). The exam is sent as a link through the email registered in the form within 3 - 7 working days.

sources.text:
International Baccalaureate (IB)
Applicant should have completed the Baccalaureate diploma degree and satisfied its general requirements. Transfer credit may be granted. Students should have 6 subjects, following these roles: 3 subjects at a higher level and 3 subjects at a standard level.
For Engineering & Applied Sciences ,Information Technology & Computer Science, and Energy and Environmental Engineering School majors: Math and Physics at a higher level are required.
For Biotechnology majors: Chemistry and Biology at a higher level are required.
For Business majors: any 3 subjects at a higher level plus the standard level.
The minimum accepted point is (24).
N.B. Students should have passed the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge subjects.

sources.title: Can I double major? What are the steps? — FAQs | Business Administration School
sources.text:
Can I double major? What are the steps?
Yes, students can pursue a double major by:
Maintaining a minimum GPA of 3.5.
Meeting the admission and graduation requirements for both majors.
Declaring the second major before their senior year.
Obtaining approval from the Program Director and Deans of both majors.
Only one degree will be awarded, and students should work closely with advisors to fulfill both majors' requirements.

The medical team provides first-aid services, emergency medical treatment of accidental injuries, as well as the transfer of complicated cases to hospitals under NU medical staff supervision and will contact the student's emergency number so the student's family would be notified. Also, NU medical team is handling medical insurance processes, follow-ups and approvals for all NU families.
Additionally, they arrange for prevention-protection programs at all university locations to maximize its environmental safety and they organize and/or supervise health-oriented activities such as: blood donation campaigns, healthy nutritional workshops, COVID-19 prevention campaigns…etc.
The clinic is equipped with all basic equipment and medicines for examination and treatment.
The clinic is open daily from 9:00 am till 10:00 pm except for Fridays from 9:00 am till 4:00 pm.

sources.title: Online teaching at Egyptian private universities during COVID 19: Lessons learned — Online teaching at Egyptian private universities during COVID 19: Lessons learned | Engineering and Applied Science School
sources.text: interviews with experienced faculty members and decision-makers (2) followed by a survey to comprehend the drivers of students’ satisfaction concerning online education throughout COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 200 replies were collected from two universities, located in west Cairo. A literature review was conducted to validate the research constructs and to support drafting the recommendations. The results show that faculty members have identified five challenges, which are: (1) course design, (2) instructor quality, (3) assessment techniques, (4) technology and e-learning platforms, and (5) students’ attitude. The survey results have proved that the first four challenges are drivers of student satisfaction, especially the assessment techniques. A list of recommendations was proposed based on the previously mentioned challenges. This was the first survey that targeted students at private universities in Cairo post- COVID-19 pandemic. The findings will be useful for preparing short to long term strategic plan focusing on blended techniques. © 2020 IEEE.

sources.title: Student Internship Report Program — Internships | NU
sources.text:
Student Internship Report Program
The internship is an integral part of your study at Nile University. It should provide you with real-life experience in your field of interest. To fulfill the academic requirements of the internship you are required to submit an internship report following the specifications outlined in this guide. This report should be submitted no longer than a week after your internship and should be handed to NU training and internship supervisor.
An Internship Report must include an outline of the business of the company for which you worked, summarize the work you did, and discuss the specific outcomes you achieved. The report must demonstrate your ability to communicate what you have done in your internship and how it relates to your academic background. The report should be typed, written in a professional way and does not exceed 15 pages (single spaced, font: Times New Roman 12).

sources.title: Summer Internship/Service-Learning Program — Internships | NU
sources.text:
Summer Internship/Service-Learning Program
Nile University undergraduate students are required to engage in an internship or service-learning experience a year before graduation. Student internships provide on-the-job training opportunities to students that help them gain experience in their fields, develop an interest in a particular career, and create a network of contacts. Service-learning enriches learning by engaging students in meaningful service to their communities. Students apply academic skills to solving real-world problems and linking their learning with genuine needs. They also learn to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to global concerns such as hunger, pollution, and diversity.
Students are required to spend around 150 hours (a full month) of non-lecture time on their internship/service-learning activity and submit a report at the end. The intern supervisor is also required to submit an evaluation report and recommend a final score/grade for the student.
Three reports are required:
- An Initial Report filled in by NU Training & Internship Executive in coordination with the company/organization before the start of the internship. This report must be approved by the Business Supervisor.
- An Intern Super

o and later expanded to several Egyptian universities. In February 2019, it was founded at Nile University, with Mohamed Yasser as the Head of Reporters.
The organization's vision is to unite and empower students across Egypt by reporting impartially on university news and raising awareness among students. It covers various fields of work, including articles, reports, investigations, photography, and events.
The Insider NU is known for its annual conference for student journalism, which brings together Insider teams from different universities. Mohamed Yasser served as the President and Editor-in-Chief of The Insider Nile University for several years, overseeing its growth and development. Under his leadership, the organization focused on media coverage, news reporting, and expanding its activities. They also launched podcasts, conducted interviews with notable figures, and initiated campaigns and events to engage students.
The Insider Nile University achieved administrative stability and notable success during Mohamed Yasser's tenure. In 2023, he stepped down from his position, marking the end of his leadership journey with The Insider Nile University.

result.answer:
Yes, the NU ICPC community offers a specific level for beginners. They provide a training program that includes a "Level 0" which is specifically designed to teach basic programming skills [1] [2] [7].

Official pages for details and updates: [ICPC](https://nu.edu.eg/students/student-activities/icpc).

sources.title: ICPC — International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) | NU
sources.text:
data structures, algorithms, dynamic programming, graphs and trees, geometry, and many other issues.
Who are we? Other than helping problem solvers and putting them on track, the community has held periodic sessions for three years now. Sessions start from teaching basic programming skills and coding languages to teaching complex algorithms and practical solving approaches, which are held every week. There are two levels this semester, and more to be added to the next one. Level 0 teaches basic programming; level 1 teaches data structures and algorithms; and Level 3 is an advanced level that the community seniors guide.
Who can join us? Anyone has a passion for learning new algorithms and is eager to compete.

sources.text:
only one computer. A set of 13-15 problems is given to each group, in a time duration of 5 hours. Each team tries to solve the maximum number of problems in the least time possible. The contest is all about problem-solving. Problems are real-world problems that require a knowledge of competitive programming topics. Those topics include data structures, algorithms, dynamic programming, graphs and trees, geometry, and many other issues.
Who are we? Other than helping problem solvers and putting them on track, the community has held periodic sessions for three years now. sources.title: ICPC — International Collegiate Programming Contest (ICPC) | NU
sources.text:
ICPC
ICPC stands for International Collegiate Programming Contest. It is an annual team-based programming competition. Only university students who haven’t turned 24 yet can compete in the ICPC contests. A single team has 3 participants, each alternate on only one computer. A set of 13-15 problems is given to each group, in a time duration of 5 hours. Each team tries to solve the maximum number of problems in the least time possible. The contest is all about problem-solving. Problems are real-world problems that require a knowledge of competitive programming topics. Those topics include data structures, algorithms, dynamic programming, graphs and trees, geometry, and many other issues.
Who are we? Other than helping problem solvers and putting them on track, the community has held periodic sessions for three years now.

sources.title: Mission — NIMUN (Nile University Model United Nations) | NU
sources.text:
Mission
NIMUN’s mission is to cultivate student awareness and enhance their understanding of the United Nations while maintaining a friendly and professional environment. NIMUN, a simulation of the United Nations hosted at Nile University, is divided into two distinct sides.
The Academic Committee side provides participants with a platform to explore politics, diplomacy, debating skills, international relations, and related subjects. Meanwhile, the Organizing Committee side enables participants to collaborate in various committees throughout the year, ensuring seamless planning and execution of the main event.
The organization strives to create a transformative experience that fosters knowledge, skill development, and an appreciation for global affairs among students.

sources.title: Mission — Wessal-NU | NU
sources.text:
Mission
The club centers around providing essential resources to individuals in need while also fostering a culture of charitable awareness among students within the university. Recognizing the transformative power of acts of kindness and selflessness, it aims to cultivate a genuine interest in philanthropy and the principles of giving back. By instilling a sense of compassion and social responsibility, it seeks to empower university students to make a positive impact on the communities and create a ripple effect of generosity that extends far beyond the university walls, contributing to the betterment of society as a whole.

sources.text:
From vision to reality: the founders’ story by (Marwa Elbadawy)
Marwa Elbadawy, a Mechatronics Engineering student, is the visionary founder of Wessal club at Nile University. Originally a student club at her previous school, Marwa felt a strong desire to continue making a positive impact and sought permission from the co-founders of Wesal to establish it at NU
.
Her goal was to inspire students to engage in acts of kindness and giving on a daily basis. Having started her journey in high school, Marwa recognized the need for a charity club at university that would instill in students the values of giving and the significance of making a difference in the community.

sources.title: From vision to reality: the founders’ story Enactus Nile University, founded by (Mohamed Asran) — Enactus-NU | NU
sources.text:
Taking decisive action, Mohamed pursued the necessary license to establish Enactus Nile University. Successfully obtaining the license, he proceeded to assemble a dedicated team.
To foster growth and garner valuable experience, Mohamed sought collaboration with Enactus branches at Helwan University and Cairo University for guidance, consultation, and training. Enactus Nile University has achieved notable success in its pursuit of developing entrepreneurial leaders and driving positive change.
Noteworthy accomplishments include participation in a comprehensive leadership training program that encompassed entrepreneurship, leadership skills, and idea testing. Furthermore, Enactus Nile University successfully revitalized the esteemed "Meshwary" training program, endorsed by UNICEF, which offers free training to university students.
These achievements exemplify Enactus Nile University's commitment to empowering students and cultivating a better world through hands-on learning.

sources.title: Missions & Objectives — Cybersecurity | Information Technology and Computer Science School
sources.text:
Missions & Objectives
The Cybersecurity program at Nile University is dedicated to preparing innovative and highly skilled graduates capable of addressing current and emerging cybersecurity challenges. Through a balanced integration of theoretical knowledge, practical application, and interdisciplinary research, the program aims to contribute to the advancement of digital security, safeguard critical infrastructure, and support national and global initiatives in cybersecurity. Emphasizing ethical responsibility and lifelong learning, the program aims to develop solutions that enhance digital trust, privacy, and societal well-being, ensuring that our graduates are prepared to make a meaningful impact in the field.

sources.title: From vision to reality: the founder’s story — Pixels NU | NU
sources.text:
From vision to reality: the founder’s story
There was a time when the university's media community faced a shortage of skilled designers, photographers, and video editors. In response to this challenge, a group of students with substantial experience in multimedia recognized the need to enhance the quality of media production on campus. They initiated a comprehensive series of workshops, intending to impart their knowledge to as many students as possible. Subsequently, these students approached the Student Union (SU) with their concept. The SU was highly impressed by the idea's potential to benefit the entire university community and pledged its support. This collaboration marked the official establishment of pixels, a club with a diverse membership working collectively to unleash the creativity of every individual.

sources.title: NIMUN (Nile University Model United Nations) — NIMUN (Nile University Model United Nations) | NU
sources.text:
NIMUN (Nile University Model United Nations)
Nile International Model United Nations (NIMUN) is a simulation of the United Nations founded in September 2015 by members of the student body for participants from within and outside Nile University. NIMUN was founded to broaden the student activity body by establishing a recreational and educational program that would provide its members with the space to grow in various areas, whether it be organizational, substantive, or managerial. The NIMUN body consists of an academic branch and an administrative branch. Both departments will adhere to your interests and aid you in utilizing your talents and enhancing them.
They aim to expand their understanding of the world around us and perhaps change something about it one day.

NIMUN’s mission is to cultivate student awareness and enhance their understanding of the United Nations while maintaining a friendly and professional environment. NIMUN, a simulation of the United Nations hosted at Nile University, is divided into two distinct sides.
The Academic Committee side provides participants with a platform to explore politics, diplomacy, debating skills, international relations, and related subjects. Meanwhile, the Organizing Committee side enables participants to collaborate in various committees throughout the year, ensuring seamless planning and execution of the main event.
The organization strives to create a transformative experience that fosters knowledge, skill development, and an appreciation for global affairs among students.

request.question: I like analyzing DNA datasets more than doing wet-lab experiments. What does NU's Bioinformatics description say about genomics and proteomics?

result.answer: Nile University's Bioinformatics program describes genomics as the sequencing and interpretation of all genomic entities, including genes and transcripts, in an organism [1] [2]. Proteomics is defined as the analysis of the entire set of proteins or proteomes [1] [2]. The program notes that Bioinformatics is the key to understanding complex biological systems because it is used by these two large-scale fields, as well as in metabolomics and transcriptomics [1] [2].

sources.title: Description — About Bioinformatics | Biotechnology School
sources.text:
Description
Bioinformatics is a new, rapidly growing science that applies computer technology to acquire, store, analyze, and disseminate biological and clinical data. Bioinformatics integrates various areas of study, including computer sciences, molecular biology, biotechnology, and mathematics.
Bioinformatics is used by two necessary large-scale fields: genomics and proteomics. Genomics points to the sequencing and interpretation of all genomic entities, including genes and transcripts, in an organism. Proteomics refers to the analysis of the entire set of proteins or proteomes. Moreover, metabolomics and transcriptomics are other areas of biology where Bioinformatics is applied. Thus, Bioinformatics is the key to understanding complex biological systems.

sources.text:
5. Bioinformatics (OPPM 105)
Course description
With the advent of technological advancements in biology came the need to develop methods for analysing high amounts of complex data. This resulted in the birth of the field known as “bioinformatics”, which is totally concerned with biological data analysis and interpretation. This course covers the basics of bioinformatics from the definitions to the operating systems and programming languages. It also covers the most commonly used bioinformatic techniques, such as phylogenetic analysis and molecular modelling, as well as their clinical applications.
Intended Learning outcomes (ILOs)
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Describe the importance of bioinformatics.
List different biological databases and their uses.
Perform advanced search of the literature.
Distinguish between different programming languages and their applications.
Analyze DNA sequences.
Design primers.
Distinguish between methods used in genetic and genomic analysis.
Demonstrate the use of genomic methods for studying human genetic variation.
Perform multiple sequence alignments.
List proteomic tools used for analyzing proteomic data.
Identify the importance

sources.text:
proteomics as a junior researcher at the Egyptian National Research Centre and Nile University.
Dr. Mysara was awarded a joint Ph.D. between KU Leuven and Vrije Universiteit Brussel under the mentorship of Prof. Jeroen Raes. His doctoral research focused on the development and application of computational tools for high-throughput metagenomics data analysis. Following his Ph.D., he completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the Lab of Medical Microbiology, University of Antwerp.
He later joined the interdisciplinary bioscience group at the Belgian Nuclear Research Centre (SCK CEN) as a senior scientist and research project leader. In 2022, he returned to Egypt to join Nile University, where he continues to advance bioinformatics research, education, and academic program development.
Dr. Mysara has authored more than 50 peer-reviewed publications in leading international journals and currently holds an h-index of 25.

sources.title: Description — About Applied Biotechnology | Biotechnology School
sources.text:
Description
Applied Biotechnology Major is an interdisciplinary field that applies technology to biology to improve the quality of human life by developing innovative products that help maintain the planet's health. Examples include bio-based vaccines, advanced and more accurate diagnostic tools for diseases in humans and animals, alternative fuels based on corn or sugar cane, crossbred harvests that resist pests, and decreased dependence on chemical pesticides.
Graduates of this major can get hired in manufacturing, pharmaceutical, chemical, healthcare, agriculture, textile industries, forensic and molecular biology labs, etc.

request.question: Does NU's software-engineering master's focus only on coding, or does it include requirements, testing and quality assurance?

result.answer: The MSc Software Engineering program at Nile University does not focus only on coding; it includes requirements management, testing, and quality assurance. Students in the program will master the principles of requirements management, analysis modeling, software architecture design, testing and verification, and quality assurance [1]. The program is designed to produce technically astute graduates with solid managerial, leadership, and communication skills to become leaders in the software industry [2].

sources.text:
The set of skills that MSc Software Engineering students will acquire are the following:
Have a solid understanding of the software development life cycle and the concepts of operation of software projects.
Possess the knowledge and practice of managing software development.
Be able to utilize the methodologies of hardware, software integration, and networking.
Master the principles of requirements management, analysis modeling, software architecture design, testing and verification, and quality assurance.

request.question: دبلومة Management of Technology في النيل طريق مقفول ولا ممكن بعدها أكمل MSc MOT؟

result.answer:
لا، دبلومة الـ Management of Technology في جامعة النيل مش طريق مقفول؛ الـ Certificate of Proficiency في الـ Management of Technology مصممة بحيث إن الـ holders بتاعها يقدروا يكملوا دراساتهم العليا (postgraduate studies) ويدخلوا الـ MSc in MOT في جامعة النيل [1] [3] [4].

البرنامج ده بيقدم تدريب عملي (hands-on training) ومبني على الـ current industry standards عشان يساعد الـ technical entrepreneurs، والـ curriculum بتاعته بتغطي الـ essential stages والـ tools الخاصة بالـ Management of Technology [1] [2] [4].

التفاصيل والتحديثات على الصفحات الرسمية: [Management of Technology Professional Diploma](https://mot.nu.edu.eg/) · [About Management of Technology Professional Diploma](https://mot.nu.edu.eg/program/management-technology-professional-diploma/about-management-technology-professional-diploma).

## Integrated Marketing Communication
This course provides an integrative approach to the study of the promotion mix, including advertising, publicity, personal selling, sales promotion and reseller support. Students will learn how the different marketing communication elements work together to enhance the marketing function and to achieve maximum impact on the marketing plan and the organization performance. Students will develop an integrated marketing communication plan for a product, service or idea using the concepts and techniques learned in class. The course also considers the latest approaches of effective public relations, by reviewing the components of a public relations campaign, and examining what has worked for others, as you craft your own form and style.

result.answer:
أيوه، تخصص الـ Operations Management and Supply Chains (OPMG) في Nile University بيغطي فعلاً مواضيع الـ procurement والـ inventory. الكورسات بتشمل دراسة الـ procurement من خلال مواضيع زي الـ purchasing و الـ material requirement planning [8]، وكمان الـ inventory من خلال دراسة الـ inventory control، الـ production planning، والـ just-in-time (JIT) systems [6].

Ever wonder how your favorite products make it from the factory to your doorstep? The
Operations and Supply Chain Management
major puts you at the heart of this exciting, fast-paced world. If you love solving problems and want to play a key role in global business, this major is your calling.

## Genetics-I
Theoretical Part: This course will be concerned with the concepts of Mendelian genetics, genetic analysis, chromosome theory, as well as all the basic chromosomal phenomena. Finally, it will introduce the different genetics of bacteria and viruses. Practical Part: This practical course will be concerned with establishing the culture of different organisms and observing their genetic variance thus applying gene analysis techniques on observational data, performing breeding, sex determination and control, explaining the transgenic organisms as well as polyploidy, mastering Mendelian randomization techniques, finally human cancer genetics will be introduced with some of the related diseases.

sources.text:
5. Bioinformatics (OPPM 105)
Course description
With the advent of technological advancements in biology came the need to develop methods for analysing high amounts of complex data. This resulted in the birth of the field known as “bioinformatics”, which is totally concerned with biological data analysis and interpretation. This course covers the basics of bioinformatics from the definitions to the operating systems and programming languages. It also covers the most commonly used bioinformatic techniques, such as phylogenetic analysis and molecular modelling, as well as their clinical applications.
Intended Learning outcomes (ILOs)
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
Describe the importance of bioinformatics.
List different biological databases and their uses.
Perform advanced search of the literature.
Distinguish between different programming languages and their applications.
Analyze DNA sequences.
Design primers.
Distinguish between methods used in genetic and genomic analysis.
Demonstrate the use of genomic methods for studying human genetic variation.
Perform multiple sequence alignments.
List proteomic tools used for analyzing proteomic data.
Identify the importance

sources.text:
Description
Master of Science in Mechatronics Engineering is one of the few interdisciplinarities serving diverse domains of application and industry. It integrates mechanical, electronics, control, and computer engineering to develop new end-user products, production systems and automated service establishments that incorporate all those interfaces together. The research topics of the master’s program fall within the categories of:
Factory and Process Automation.
Advanced and Embedded Techniques in the Design and Development of Mechatronic Systems,
Robotic Applications,
Unmanned Vehicles,
Advanced Control Algorithms,
Control Techniques for Dynamic Systems,
Adaptive Structures,
Smart Materials and Structures,
Optimization of Discrete-Event Systems.

## Dr. Mohamed Ahmed Afifi
## Assistant Professor
Dr. Mohamed Afifi is a faculty member of the Mechanical Engineering program and SESC research centre, specializing in metallurgy, thermomechanical processing, and the characterization of metallic materials. With a distinguished career that includes a pivotal role at Brunel University London, focusing on developing light-weight high strength metallic materials for the automotive sector, and a PhD from the Beijing Institute of Technology. Dr. Afifi's work adeptly bridges the gap between academic research and industrial application, evidenced by his numerous contributions to leading journals in materials science.

## Valorization of Shrimp shells and Agricultural Wastes for Sustainable Biopolymer-Based Packaging Solutions
## Abstract
This research project focused on the valorization of shrimp shell and agricultural waste materials, such as rice straw, for the development of sustainable biopolymer-based packaging solutions. The key objectives were to extract and optimize chitosan and other biopolymers from shrimp shells, and to reinforce these materials with chitin fibers and whiskers for enhanced mechanical and barrier properties.

## Bio-inspired Soft Robot for Monitoring Coral Reefs
## Abstract
Coral reefs play a crucial role in supporting a quarter of all aquatic life, but their existence is now threatened by ongoing climate changes. Our project aims to develop an underwater soft robot that can mimic the morphology and shape of actual marine creatures and to imitate their swimming motion. This robot can play a critical role as monitoring platform to understand the reefs environment more without doing much disturbance in such delicate environment.

ASRT

request.question: What is the NU shrimp-shell packaging project trying to extract, and why reinforce it with chitin fibers?

result.answer:
The NU shrimp-shell packaging project aims to extract and optimize chitosan and other biopolymers from shrimp shells [1] [2] [3] [9]. The project also utilizes agricultural waste materials, such as rice straw, to develop sustainable biopolymer-based packaging solutions [1] [2] [3] [9].

These materials are reinforced with chitin fibers and whiskers to enhance their mechanical and barrier properties [1] [2] [3] [9]. Specifically, the addition of chitin fibers and whiskers to chitosan composites improves tensile strength, Young's modulus, and thermal degradation temperature, making the composite thin films suitable for thermal applications and as a promising replacement for synthetic plastic polymers [7].

result.answer:
مركز الابتكار وريادة الأعمال والتنافسية (IECC) في جامعة النيل بيقدم خدمة "Venture Clienting" للشركات عشان تساعدهم يلاقوا حلول مبتكرة. الخدمة دي بتشمل تحديد احتياجات البيزنس، وتحديد الأهداف، والبحث عن الشركات الناشئة (startups) اللي عندها تكنولوجيا واعدة ومناسبة لاحتياجات الشركة [2].

المركز بيساعد الشركات من خلال عدة خطوات: البحث عن الحلول المناسبة، وإجراء فحص دقيق (due diligence) للشركات الناشئة، وإدارة مشاريع تجريبية (pilot projects) عشان يتم اختبار الحلول في أرض الواقع [4]. بعد نجاح التجربة، المركز بيساعد في دمج الحلول دي في الشركة وتوسيع نطاقها، وكمان بيوفر فرص للتعاون الاستراتيجي والوصول لشبكة واسعة من الشركات الناشئة [3] [4].

sources.text:
Nile University’s IECC Concludes Faculty Track Entrepreneurship Program, Showcasing Groundbreaking Startups from Academic Research
Nile University’s Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Competitiveness Centre (IECC) wraps up its 10-week
Entrepreneurship Program – Faculty Track
, empowering faculty to convert cutting-edge research into viable startups.
Four innovative ventures emerged, spanning advanced materials, AI education, bio-inspired tech, and sustainable construction, pitched to a distinguished panel last week.
The program highlights strategies for “research commercialization” (tech transfer and IP protection), “skill bridging” (entrepreneurial training), and “impact scaling” (market validation and funding pathways), aligning with Egypt’s national innovation agenda.
Nile University today

request.question: IECC بيقول إن اختيار startup مناسب للشركة بياخد تقريبًا قد إيه؟ وهل ده شامل التنفيذ؟

result.answer:
الـ IECC (Innovation Entrepreneurship and Competitiveness Centre) في Nile University مش بيحددوا وقت معين لاختيار الـ startup المناسب للشركة، لكنهم بيركزوا على تقديم دعم شامل للـ innovators والـ co-founders عشان يسدوا الـ resource gaps. الـ center بيقدم خدمات متنوعة بتشمل الـ innovation management، والـ entrepreneurial journey support، والـ technology and business model advising، وكمان الـ product design، والـ engineering development and validation، والـ go-to market strategy [1] [6] [9].

بالنسبة للتنفيذ، الـ IECC بيقدم دعم في الـ engineering development و الـ validation، وكمان بيساعد في تحويل الـ academic projects لـ real-world business ventures [1] [7]. كمان عندهم برامج زي الـ ClimaTech Accelerator اللي بتدعم الـ ventures في مجالات تقنية محددة [3].

التفاصيل والتحديثات على الصفحات الرسمية: [Innovation Entrepreneurship and competitiveness Centre  IECC , is Nile University’s leading center t](https://iecc.nu.edu.eg/news/suez-canal-bank-and-central-bank-of-egypt-select-top-startups-for-fifth-edition-of-launch-saas-technological-applications-business-incubator/) · [Nile University Launches ClimaTech Accelerator 2025 to Empower Plastic Circular Economy Startups](https://iecc.nu.edu.eg/news/climatech-cycle3-launchevent-2025/) · [Innovation Entrepreneurship and competitiveness Centre  IECC , is Nile University’s leading center t](https://iecc.nu.edu.eg/news/nile-universitys-iecc-concludes-faculty-track-entrepreneurship-program-showcasing-groundbreaking-startups-from-academic-research/) · [IECC Entrepreneurship Program – Undergrad Track Concludes Its Third and Final Round](https://iecc.nu.edu.eg/news/iecc-entrepreneurship-program-undergrad-track-concludes-its-third-and-final-round/) · [About Us - IECC](https://iecc.nu.edu.eg/about-us/).

sources.text:
Nile University’s IECC Concludes Faculty Track Entrepreneurship Program, Showcasing Groundbreaking Startups from Academic Research
Nile University’s Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Competitiveness Centre (IECC) wraps up its 10-week
Entrepreneurship Program – Faculty Track
, empowering faculty to convert cutting-edge research into viable startups.
Four innovative ventures emerged, spanning advanced materials, AI education, bio-inspired tech, and sustainable construction, pitched to a distinguished panel last week.
The program highlights strategies for “research commercialization” (tech transfer and IP protection), “skill bridging” (entrepreneurial training), and “impact scaling” (market validation and funding pathways), aligning with Egypt’s national innovation agenda.
Nile University today

Once the nominated students receive acceptance from the partner university, students should apply for these scholarships and submit their applications before the deadline.

Nile University does not offer any kind of fund\scholarship for exchange students. Exchange students will be responsible for paying NU tuition fees at NU. Students will also be responsible for paying their living expenses related to their participation in this program including:
Flight Tickets
Accommodation
Medical insurance
Meals
Visa Fees
Transportation
Supplies
Other Funding/Scholarships Opportunities:
There are partner universities with NU offering Erasmus Grants to cover the travel costs and the monthly living expenses. Also, there are National Agencies abroad offering scholarships and funds to cover the exchange semester. Once the nominated students receive acceptance from the partner university, students should apply for these scholarships and submit their applications before the deadline.
Note:
Students expect to receive the scholarship amounts once they arrive at their partner universities so students should prepare themselves to cover the costs before arrival such as:
Flight Tickets
Visa Fees
Health Insurance, if required
Accommodation Fees, if required

## Health Service
## Health Service
The NU clinic - located on the ground floor of the UB2 Building - offers professional medical services to all NU community members by qualified university doctors and nurses.
The medical team provides first-aid services, emergency medical treatment of accidental injuries, as well as the transfer of complicated cases to hospitals under NU medical staff supervision and will contact the student's emergency number so the student's family would be notified. Also, NU medical team is handling medical insurance processes, follow-ups and approvals for all NU families.
Additionally, they arrange for prevention-protection programs at all university locations to maximize its environmental safety and they organize and/or supervise health-oriented activities such as: blood donation campaigns, healthy nutritional workshops, COVID-19 prevention campaigns…etc.
The clinic is equipped with all basic equipment and medicines for examination and treatment.
The clinic is open daily from 9:00 am till 10:00 pm except for Fridays from 9:00 am till 4:00 pm.

sources.title: From vision to reality: the founder’s story — Pixels NU | NU
sources.text:
From vision to reality: the founder’s story
There was a time when the university's media community faced a shortage of skilled designers, photographers, and video editors. In response to this challenge, a group of students with substantial experience in multimedia recognized the need to enhance the quality of media production on campus. They initiated a comprehensive series of workshops, intending to impart their knowledge to as many students as possible. Subsequently, these students approached the Student Union (SU) with their concept. The SU was highly impressed by the idea's potential to benefit the entire university community and pledged its support. This collaboration marked the official establishment of pixels, a club with a diverse membership working collectively to unleash the creativity of every individual.

sources.title: Do I need an English language qualification test to apply for NU? — FAQs | NU
sources.text:
Do I need an English language qualification test to apply for NU?
All applying students must show proof of English proficiency by achieving the level indicated in one of three testing alternatives below:
A score of 61 or above in the IBT (Internet-based TOEFL).
A score of 6 or above in the IELTS taken at the British Council.
A score of B1 or above in the Oxford exam (no retakes for this exam and is costs 300 EGP). The exam is sent as a link through the email registered in the form within 3 - 7 working days.

request.question: يعني إيه correlation مش causation؟ اديني مثال بسيط من حضور المحاضرات والدرجات.

result.answer:
بص يا سيدي، جملة "Correlation is not causation" معناها إن وجود علاقة إحصائية (correlation) بين حاجتين مش معناه بالضرورة إن واحدة منهم هي السبب (cause) في وقوع التانية. يعني ممكن حاجتين يحصلوا مع بعض في نفس الوقت لسبب تالت خالص، أو مجرد صدفة.

بالنسبة لمثالك عن حضور المحاضرات والدرجات:
ممكن تلاقي إن الطلاب اللي بيحضروا المحاضرات (Attendance) بيجيبوا درجات عالية (High grades). هنا في "Correlation" واضح جداً. لكن ده مش معناه إن مجرد "وجودك" في القاعة هو اللي رفع درجتك. السبب الحقيقي (Causation) ممكن يكون إن الطالب "المهتم" بالمادة هو اللي بيكرر حضور المحاضرات وفي نفس الوقت بيذاكر كويس، فـ الاهتمام هو الـ root cause للاتنين.

request.question: Explain the difference between a citation and plagiarism in plain language, without inventing a university policy.

result.answer:
In simple terms, the difference comes down to honesty and credit. 

A **citation** is when you give credit to the original author of an idea, fact, or quote. It is a way of saying, "I didn't come up with this myself; here is where I found it." It allows you to use outside information while still being honest about where that information originated.

**Plagiarism**, on the other hand, is using someone else's words or ideas and pretending they are your own. It happens when you fail to provide a citation. Even if it's just a small part of your work or a slight paraphrase, if you don't credit the source, it's considered plagiarism. Think of it as "copying" without permission or acknowledgment.

I'm built specifically for Nile University, Egypt. This general answer isn't verified against university sources.

request.question: 3ayez checklist 3 points 3ashan a3raf en el survey question mesh leading question.

result.answer:
بص يا سيدي، عشان تتأكد إن السؤال مش "leading" (يعني مبيوجهش اللي بيجاوب لقرار معين)، خد بالك من الـ 3 نقط دول:

1. **الحيادية في الصياغة:** ابعد عن أي كلمات فيها رأي شخصي أو صفات قوية. مثلاً بدل ما تقول "إيه رأيك في الخدمة الممتازة اللي بنقدمها؟"، خليها "إيه تقييمك لمستوى الخدمة؟".
2. **تعدد الاختيارات (Balanced Options):** لو السؤال فيه اختيارات (Multiple Choice)، لازم تكون متوازنة. يعني لو فيه اختيار "موافق"، لازم يكون فيه "غير موافق"، بدل ما تحط "موافق" و "موافق جداً" بس.
3. **تجنب الافتراضات:** ماتفترضش إن الشخص عنده وجهة نظر معينة. بدل "ليه أنت بتحب المنتج بتاعنا؟" (اللي بتفترض إنه بيحبه)، خليها "إيه رأيك في المنتج بتاعنا؟".

لو محتاجني أراجع معاك أسئلة معينة، ابعتها وأنا أقولك لو محتاجة تعديل ولا لأ.
